text: On a cool Saturday at the Eddlestone Dog Trials, a border collie named Bracken of Mirehall took best in show, drawing applause from a crowd that had gathered under low grey clouds beside the old sports field. Handled by Mera Lint, the three-year-old dog impressed judges with what they called “clean movement, calm focus and rare obedience under pressure.” The annual trials, now in their 41st year, began as a small parish event to raise money for fence repairs and have grown into one of Northfold’s steadier summer fixtures. This year 27 dogs competed across sheepwork, recall and agility, with Bracken finishing ahead of a smooth-coated retriever and a black sheepdog from West Fen.
